en.title: Total Number of Days That Reach the Maximum Online Count
en.description:
User i is online every day from login[i] to logout[i], inclusive at both ends; on the same day, logins happen before logouts. Find how many days have an online count equal to the global maximum online count; do not return the count itself.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains login, and the third line contains logout. 1≤n≤100000, 0≤login[i]≤logout[i]≤100000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 1 and 2 respectively. In the first example, days 2 and 3 both have two users online; in the third example, two non-adjacent days both reach the peak of 1.
hints: Use a difference array: add 1 at login and subtract 1 at logout+1, scan 0..100000, and update the maximum count and the number of days that reach it.
